nodes.notes: Adapter pattern (like Gmail): the pipeline, guardrails and telemetry are untouched - A2A leads are born instrumented.

parameters.query:
WITH ins AS (INSERT INTO vaibhavcapstone_a2a_tasks (task_id, lead_id, business_id, remote_agent)
  VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4) ON CONFLICT (task_id) DO NOTHING RETURNING task_id),
ev AS (INSERT INTO vaibhavcapstone_events (business_id, lead_id, trace_id, agent, action, actor, detail)
  VALUES ($3, $2, NULL, 'a2a-server', 'A2A_TASK_CREATED', $4, jsonb_build_object('task_id', $1)) RETURNING event_id)
SELECT $1 AS task_id;

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: '2.0', id: $('Build Task Id').first().json.rpc_id, result: { id: $('Build Task Id').first().json.task_id, contextId: $('Build Task Id').first().json.task_id, kind: 'task', status: { state: 'submitted', timestamp: new Date().toISOString() } } }) }}

parameters.query:
SELECT t.task_id, l.status, l.status_detail, b.name AS business_name,
  d.subject AS reply_subject, d.body AS reply_body, r.items
FROM vaibhavcapstone_a2a_tasks t
JOIN vaibhavcapstone_leads l USING (lead_id)
JOIN vaibhavcapstone_businesses b ON b.business_id = t.business_id
LEFT JOIN vaibhavcapstone_drafts d ON d.lead_id = l.lead_id AND d.draft_type = 'CUSTOMER' AND d.status = 'SENT'
LEFT JOIN vaibhavcapstone_recommendations r ON r.lead_id = l.lead_id
WHERE t.task_id = $1 AND t.business_id = $2;

parameters.query: SELECT COALESCE((SELECT $1 = 'Bearer ' || value FROM vaibhavcapstone_platform_config WHERE key = 'a2a_bearer'), false) AS authorized;

nodes.name: Verify Bearer
nodes.notes: Token lives in vaibhavcapstone_platform_config (inserted at deploy from .env, never committed). Code nodes cannot read env vars in this n8n - DB is the source of truth anyway.

parameters.content:
## The robot door — letting another company's AI buy from us

Everything else in this system serves a person. This door serves software: another organisation's AI agent, shopping on its owner's behalf, with nobody writing an email on either side.

It speaks a shared language for AI agents, so a buyer's agent and our seller's agent can do business **without either company having built anything for the other.**

### The public business card — no password needed

Any agent may ask: who are you, what do you sell, how do I talk to you? We answer from this business's own record — and include one line that matters more than the rest: **a human reviews every offer before it is released.** We advertise the gate rather than hide it.

### Someone knocks

**A request arrives.** We work out what is being asked: send a new enquiry, or check how an existing one is getting on. Anything else is refused politely.

**Check the caller's key.** The business card is public, but *doing business* needs a shared key. No key, no conversation.

Note that the refusal is written in the protocol's own language rather than as a plain web error — a machine on the other end needs an answer it can actually understand.

### The work — through the very same pipeline

**A new enquiry** is handed to the front door, exactly as an email would be, and the buyer's agent gets a ticket number to check on later.

Nothing downstream knows or cares that this one came from a machine. Same reading, same scoring, same grounded products, same human approval.

**Checking on an enquiry** simply looks up how far it has got.

### Answering in the agent's own language

Our internal stages are translated into the words the protocol uses. Most of them simply mean "working".

The one that matters: **waiting for human approval becomes "input-required"** — the standard way of saying *a person must act before this can go further*. The buyer's agent sees the human gate, understands it, and waits.

Sent becomes "completed", returned with the approved reply and a tidy list of products the other company's systems can file automatically.

## Why this door exists at all — and only here

Inside the platform, our own steps don't need a protocol to talk to each other. They're one system; they can just call each other directly. Using a formal protocol internally would be pure overhead.

At the boundary it's the opposite: the other side is a stranger, built by someone we've never spoken to. That is exactly the problem this protocol solves — so it's used here, and nowhere else.

Proven end to end on both businesses. It also flushed out a real bug: a customer asking for "journals" wasn't matching a product called "Leather Journal A5".
